1210.text:
Assertion : We use a thick wire in the secondary of a step down transformer to reduce the production heat.
Reason : When the plane of the armature is parallel to the line of force of magnetic field, the magnitude of induced e.m.f. is maximum.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
1210.sol: A step-down transformer converts electrical energy from a high voltage to one at a low voltage. Accordingly the current in the secondary will be larger than that in the primary. In order to produce less heat in the secondary, we use a wire of lesser resistance i.e. thick wire. We also know that when the plane of the armature is parallel to the lines of force of magnetic field, the rate of change of magnetic flux linked with it is maximum. Therefore the e.m.f. induced in the armature in this orientation is maximum.

3322.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
3322.text: The first ionization enthalpies of $Mg$ and $Al$ can be expected to be
3322.sol: Magnesium has the atomic number of $12$. It has the electronic configuration of~$\left[Ne\right]3s^{2}$. It has the fully filled orbitals. So, it has the high ionisation energy. The atomic number of the aluminium is $13$. It has the electronic configuration of~$\left[Ne\right]3s^{2}3p^{1}$. It has the low value of the first ionisation energy. So, the first ionisation energy of magnesium is higher than the aluminium because magnesium has the fully filled orbital. Hence,~The first ionization enthalpies of $Mg and Al$ can be expected to be~${IE}_{1} ( Mg ) = 737 . 7kJ . {mol}^{- 1}, {IE}_{1} ( Al ) = 577 . 5kJ . {mol}^{- 1}$.

6560.text: The coefficient of x^5 in $\left(3+x+x^2\right)^6$ is
6560.sol:
Since, the general term in the expansion $\left(3+x+x^2\right)^6=\frac{6!}{p!q!r!} 3^p \cdot x^q \cdot\left(x^2\right)^r$, where $p+q+r=6=\frac{6!.3^p \cdot x^{q+2 r}}{p!q!r!}$, where, $p+q+r=6$
Since, $q+2 r=5 \Rightarrow q=5-2 r$
and, $p+5-2 r+r=6 \Rightarrow p=1+r$
If $r=0 \Rightarrow p=1, q=5$. If $r=1 \Rightarrow p=2, q=3$
If $r=2 \Rightarrow p=3, q=1$. So, co-efficient of $x^5=\frac{6!3^1}{1!.5!\cdot .0!}+\frac{6!3^2}{2!.3!\cdot 1!}+\frac{6!.3^3}{3!\cdot 1!\cdot 2!}=18+540+1620=2178$

Now slope of line~${L}_{1}$~is& ${m}_{1} = cos\theta$~and slope of line& ${L}_{2}$~is& ${m}_{2} = \dfrac{cos\theta + tan\alpha}{1 - cos\theta . tan\alpha}$

Now we know that angle between two line is given by~$tanϕ = \left|\dfrac{{m}_{2} - {m}_{1}}{1 + {m}_{1}{m}_{2}}\right|$

$⇒ tan\phi = \left|\dfrac{\dfrac{cos\theta + tan\alpha}{1 - cos\theta . tan\alpha} - cos\theta}{1 + \dfrac{cos\theta + tan\alpha}{1 - cos\theta . tan\alpha} \times cos\theta}\right|$

$⇒ tan\phi = \left|\dfrac{cos\theta + tan\alpha - cos\theta + {cos}^{2}\theta . tan\alpha}{1 - cos\theta . tan\alpha + {cos}^{2}\theta + tan\alpha . cos\theta}\right|$

$⇒ tan\phi = \left|\dfrac{tan\alpha\left(1 + {cos}^{2}\theta\right)}{1 + {cos}^{2}\theta}\right|$

$⇒ tan\phi = tan\alpha$

$⇒ \phi = \alpha$

13548.text: An AC source of angular frequency $\omega$ is fed across a resistor $R$ and a capacitor $C$ in series. The current flowing in the circuit found to be $I$. Now the frequency of the source is changed to $\frac{\omega}{3}$, (maintaining the same voltage) the current in the circuit is found to be halved. What is the ratio of reactance to resistance at the original frequency?
13548.sol:
At angular frequency $\omega$, current through resistance R and capacitance C is given by
$I_{\mathrm{rms}}=\frac{V_{\mathrm{rms}}}{\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2}}=\frac{V_{\mathrm{rms}}}{\sqrt{R^2+\left(\frac{1}{\omega C}\right)^2}}$...(i)
When angular frequency is changed to $\frac{\omega}{3}$, then the current becomes $\frac{I_{\mathrm{rms}}}{2}=\frac{V_{\mathrm{rms}}}{\sqrt{R^2+\left(\frac{1}{\frac{\omega}{3} C}\right)^2}}=\frac{V_{\mathrm{rms}}}{\sqrt{R^2+\left(\frac{3}{\omega C}\right)^2}}...($ ii) Dividing Eq. (i) by Eq. (ii), we get
$\begin{array}{rlrl} & & 2=\frac{\sqrt{R^2+\left(\frac{3}{\omega C}\right)^2}}{\sqrt{R^2+\left(\frac{1}{\omega C}\right)^2}} \\ & \Rightarrow & 4\left[R^2+\left(\frac{1}{\omega C}\right)^2\right] & =R^2+\left(\frac{3}{\omega C}\right)^2 \\ & \Rightarrow & 3 R^2 & =\frac{5}{\omega^2 C^2} \\ & \Rightarrow & \frac{1}{\omega_C} & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{5}} \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{X_C}{R} & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{5}}\end{array}$

& T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{1225 \times 10^{-4}}{10^{-5} \times 121}}=2 \times3.14 \times3.181 \\ \text{ and } T=19.98 \cong 20 \mathrm{ s}

19472.text: Consider the series of reactions given and identify the final product [Z].
19472.sol:
The starting material is 2-methylpropan-2-ol. Treatment with 20% $H_3PO_4$ causes acid-catalyzed dehydration to form 2-methylpropene [W].

$(CH_3)_3C-OH \xrightarrow{H^+}$ (CH_3)_2C=CH_2$

19727.subject: Chemistry
19727.text: Among the following compounds, the most acidic is :
19727.sol:
The acidity of benzoic acid derivatives is determined by the electronic effects of the substituents present on the benzene ring.

The nitro group ($-NO_2$) is a strong electron-withdrawing group (EWG) due to both its negative inductive effect ($-I$) and negative resonance effect ($-M$). The methoxy group ($-OCH_3$) is an electron-donating group (EDG) due to its positive resonance effect ($+M$), which outweighs its negative inductive effect ($-I$) at the para position.

Comparing the given compounds:
1. 4-methoxybenzoic acid: The $-OCH_3$ group decreases the acidity of benzoic acid by donating electron density into the ring.
2. Benzoic acid: This is the reference compound.
3. 4-nitrobenzoic acid: The $-NO_2$ group increases the acidity of benzoic acid significantly due to its strong electron-withdrawing nature.
4. 3,4-dinitrobenzoic acid: This compound contains two $-NO_2$ groups. Both groups exert strong electron-withdrawing effects ($-I$ and $-M$). The presence of two such groups makes the carboxylate anion significantly more stable than in the case of 4-nitrobenzoic acid, thereby making 3,4-dinitrobenzoic acid the most acidic among the choices.

Answer: 3, 4-dinitrobenzoic acid

21515.subject: Mathematics
21515.text: Evaluate the value of the arbitrary constant ' c ' given that $\mathrm{y}(0)=0$, of the differential equation $\dfrac{d y}{d x}+\dfrac{x y}{x^2-1}=\dfrac{x^6+4 x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$
21515.sol:
The given differential equation is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x)$, where $P(x) = \dfrac{x}{x^2-1}$ and $Q(x) = \dfrac{x^6+4x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.

The integrating factor $IF$ is given by $e^{\int P(x) dx} = e^{\int \dfrac{x}{x^2-1} dx} = e^{\dfrac{1}{2} \ln|x^2-1|} = \sqrt{|x^2-1|}$.

Since the domain involves $\sqrt{1-x^2}$, we consider $|x| < 1$, so $x^2-1 < 0$. Thus, $IF = \sqrt{1-x^2}$.

Multiplying the differential equation by $IF$, we get $\dfrac{d}{dx}(y \sqrt{1-x^2}) = \dfrac{x^6+4x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \cdot \sqrt{1-x^2} = x^6+4x$.

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we have $y \sqrt{1-x^2} = \int (x^6+4x) dx = \dfrac{x^7}{7} + 2x^2 + c$.

Given the initial condition $y(0) = 0$, we substitute $x=0$ and $y=0$ into the equation: $0 \cdot \sqrt{1-0} = \dfrac{0^7}{7} + 2(0)^2 + c$.

This yields $0 = 0 + 0 + c$, which implies $c = 0$.

Answer: 0

21930.subject: Mathematics
21930.text: In a trial, the probability of success is twice the probability of failure. In six trials, the probability of at most two failure will be
21930.sol:
Let $p$ be the probability of success and $q$ be the probability of failure. Given $p = 2q$. Since $p + q = 1$, we have $2q + q = 1$, which implies $3q = 1$, so $q = \dfrac{1}{3}$ and $p = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

The number of trials is $n = 6$. We want the probability of at most two failures, which is $P(X \le 2)$ where $X$ is the number of failures. This is given by $P(X = 0) + P(X = 1) + P(X = 2)$.

Using the binomial distribution formula $P(X = k) = ^{n}C_{k} q^{k} p^{n-k}$:

$P(X = 0) = ^{6}C_{0} \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{0} \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^{6} = 1 \times 1 \times \dfrac{64}{729} = \dfrac{64}{729}$

$P(X = 1) = ^{6}C_{1} \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{1} \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^{5} = 6 \times \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{32}{243} = 2 \times \dfrac{32}{243} = \dfrac{64}{243} = \dfrac{192}{729}$

$P(X = 2) = ^{6}C_{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{2} \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^{4} = 15 \times \dfrac{1}{9} \times \dfrac{16}{81} = \dfrac{15 \times 16}{729} = \dfrac{240}{729}$

Summing these probabilities: $P(X \le 2) = \dfrac{64 + 192 + 240}{729} = \dfrac{496}{729}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{496}{729}$

22440.subject: Physics
22440.text:
The difference in energy levels of an electron at two excited levels is $13.75 \mathrm{ eV}$. If it makes a transition from the higher energy level to the lower energy level then what will be the wave length of the emitted radiation?
[given $h=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{ m}^2 \mathrm{ kg} \mathrm{ s}^{-1} ; c=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1} ; 1 \mathrm{ eV}=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{ J}$]
22440.sol:
The energy difference between the two levels is given by $\Delta E = 13.75 \text{ eV}$.

Converting this energy into Joules:
$\Delta E = 13.75 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J} = 22 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J}$.

The relationship between energy and wavelength is $\Delta E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$.

Rearranging for wavelength $\lambda$:
$\lambda = \dfrac{hc}{\Delta E}$.

Substituting the given values $h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J s}$ and $c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$:
$\lambda = \dfrac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{22 \times 10^{-19}}$.

$\lambda = \dfrac{19.8 \times 10^{-26}}{22 \times 10^{-19}} = 0.9 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.

Converting to Angstroms ($\text{A}$):
$\lambda = 0.9 \times 10^{-7} \times 10^{10} \text{ A} = 0.9 \times 10^3 \text{ A} = 900 \text{ A}$.

Answer: $900^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{A}$

23200.subject: Physics
23200.text: A man standing in a truck moving with constant velocity throws a ball vertically into air, ball falls
options: Exactly in the hand of the boy
In the truck behind the boy
In the truck ahead of the boy
23200.sol:
The truck is moving with a constant velocity $v$ in the horizontal direction. When the man throws the ball vertically upward, the ball possesses the same initial horizontal velocity $v$ as the truck and the man.

Since there is no horizontal acceleration acting on the ball (ignoring air resistance), its horizontal velocity remains constant at $v$ throughout the flight.

The truck also continues to move with the same constant horizontal velocity $v$.

Because both the ball and the truck cover the same horizontal distance in the same time interval, the ball remains directly above the point from which it was thrown relative to the truck.

Therefore, the ball falls exactly back into the hand of the man.

Answer: Exactly in the hand of the boy

23271.subject: Physics
23271.text: The radius of a nucleus as measured by electron scattering is $4.8 \mathrm{ fm}$. The mass number of nucleus is most likely to be
23271.sol:
The radius of a nucleus $R$ is related to its mass number $A$ by the formula $R = R_{0} A^{1/3}$, where $R_{0} \approx 1.2 \text{ fm}$.

Given $R = 4.8 \text{ fm}$, we have $4.8 = 1.2 \times A^{1/3}$.

Dividing both sides by $1.2$, we get $A^{1/3} = \dfrac{4.8}{1.2} = 4$.

Cubing both sides, $A = 4^{3} = 64$.

Answer: 64

23278.subject: Physics
23278.text: Which of the following statement is true when a gamma decay occurs from the nucleus of an atom?
options: Mass number is reduced by 4 and atomic number is reduced by 2
Mass number is reduced by 4 and atomic number remains the same
Mass number remains the same and atomic number increases by 1
Mass number and atomic number are not changed
23278.sol:
Gamma decay involves the emission of high-energy electromagnetic radiation, known as gamma rays, from an excited nucleus to a lower energy state.

During this process, the nucleus does not lose any protons or neutrons. Consequently, the number of protons (atomic number, $Z$) and the total number of nucleons (mass number, $A$) remain unchanged.

The transition is represented as: _Z^{A}X^{*} \rightarrow _Z^{A}X + \gamma$.

Therefore, both the mass number and the atomic number remain constant.

Answer: Mass number and atomic number are not changed$

23469.subject: Physics
23469.text: A Si and a Ge diode has identical physical dimensions. The band gap in Si is larger than that in Ge. On applying identical reverse bias across these diodes,
options: The reverse current in Ge is larger than that in Si.
The reverse current in Ge is lesser than that in Si.
The relative magnitudes of reverse currents cannot be determined from the given data.
The reverse current is identical in both cases.
23469.sol:
The reverse saturation current $I_0$ in a p-n junction diode is primarily due to the thermally generated minority charge carriers. The concentration of these minority carriers is proportional to $n_i^2$, where $n_i$ is the intrinsic carrier concentration.

The intrinsic carrier concentration $n_i$ is given by the relation $n_i^2 = A T^3 \exp \left(-\dfrac{E_g}{kT}\right), where $E_g$ is the band gap energy, $k$ is the Boltzmann constant, and $T$ is the absolute temperature.

Since the band gap $E_g$ of Silicon (Si) is approximately 1.1$ eV and that of Germanium (Ge) is approximately $0.7$ eV, we have $E_{g, Si} > E_{g, Ge}$.

Substituting these values into the expression for $n_i^2$, it follows that $n_{i, Ge}^2 > n_{i, Si}^2$ at a given temperature $T$.

Consequently, the reverse saturation current $I_0$, which depends on the concentration of minority carriers, is significantly larger for Germanium than for Silicon. Therefore, the reverse current in Ge is larger than that in Si.

Answer: The reverse current in Ge is larger than that in Si.

23580.subject: Physics
23580.text: From the following $p$-V diagram, an ideal gas undergoing a change of state from $A$ to $B$. Four different processes I, II, III and IV as shown in the figure may lead to same change of state.
options: Work done is minimum in case II
Change in internal energy is same in all the four cases
Change in internal energy is same in IV and III cases, but not in I and II
23580.sol:
The internal energy $U$ of an ideal gas is a state function, which depends only on the temperature $T$ of the gas. For an ideal gas, the internal energy is given by $U = \dfrac{f}{2} nRT$, where $f$ is the degrees of freedom.

Since the change of state is from $A$ to $B$ in all four processes, the initial state $(P_A, V_A, T_A)$ and the final state $(P_B, V_B, T_B)$ are the same for all paths.

The change in internal energy $\Delta U$ is given by $\Delta U = U_B - U_A = \dfrac{f}{2} nR(T_B - T_A)$.

Because $T_A$ and $T_B$ are fixed for all four processes, the change in internal energy $\Delta U$ must be the same for all four processes I, II, III, and IV.

Answer: Change in internal energy is same in all the four cases

24133.subject: Mathematics
24133.text: What is the value of $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} \min\{1 - x, 1 - x^3\}\, dx$?
24133.sol:
Let $I = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} \min\{1 - x, 1 - x^3\} \, dx$.

We can rewrite the integrand using the property $\min\{a - b, a - c\} = a - \max\{b, c\}$.

Thus, $\min\{1 - x, 1 - x^3\} = 1 - \max\{x, x^3\}$.

The integral becomes:

$I = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} (1 - \max\{x, x^3\}) \, dx = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} 1 \, dx - \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} \max\{x, x^3\} \, dx$

The first integral is simply:

$\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} 1 \, dx = [x]_{-1}^{2} = 2 - (-1) = 3$

To evaluate the second integral, we determine the intervals where $x \ge x^3$ and $x^3 \ge x$ by analyzing the sign of $x - x^3 = x(1 - x)(1 + x)$. The roots are $-1, 0, 1$.

In $[-1,0]$, $x^3 \ge x \Rightarrow \max\{x, x^3\} = x^3$

In $[0,1]$, $x \ge x^3 \Rightarrow \max\{x, x^3\} = x$

In $[1,2]$, $x^3 \ge x \Rightarrow \max\{x, x^3\} = x^3$

Now, we split the second integral over these intervals:

$\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} \max\{x, x^3\} \, dx = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{0} x^3 \, dx + \displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} x \, dx + \displaystyle\int_{1}^{2} x^3 \, dx$

$= \left[ \dfrac{x^4}{4} \right]_{-1}^{0} + \left[ \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{1} + \left[ \dfrac{x^4}{4} \right]_{1}^{2}$

$= \left( 0 - \dfrac{1}{4} \right) + \left( \dfrac{1}{2} -0 \right) + \left( \dfrac{16}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} \right)

$= $-\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{2}{4} + \dfrac{15}{4} = \dfrac{16}{4} =4$

Substituting this back into the expression for $I$:

$I = 3 - 4 = -1$

Answer: $-1$

27022.subject: Chemistry
27022.text:
Iodoform test can differentiate between
A. Methanol and Ethanol
B. $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COOH}$ and $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{COOH}$
C. Cyclohexene and cyclohexanone
D. Diethyl ether and Pentan-3-one
E. Anisole and acetone
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
27022.sol:
The iodoform test is given by compounds containing the methyl ketone group ($CH_3CO-$) or alcohols that can be oxidized to methyl ketones ($CH_3CH(OH)-$).
A. Methanol ($CH_3OH$) does not give the test, while Ethanol ($CH_3CH_2OH$) gives a positive iodoform test because it contains the $CH_3CH(OH)-$ group. Thus, they can be differentiated.
B. Acetic acid ($CH_3COOH$) and Propanoic acid ($CH_3CH_2COOH$) both do not give the iodoform test. Carboxylic acids generally do not respond to this test. Thus, they cannot be differentiated.
C. Cyclohexene and cyclohexanone both do not give the iodoform test. Cyclohexanone lacks a methyl group adjacent to the carbonyl carbon. Thus, they cannot be differentiated.
D. Diethyl ether ($CH_3CH_2OCH_2CH_3$) and Pentan-3-one ($CH_3CH_2COCH_2CH_3$) both do not give the iodoform test. Thus, they cannot be differentiated.
E. Anisole ($C_6H_5OCH_3$) does not give the test, while Acetone ($CH_3COCH_3$) gives a positive iodoform test as it is a methyl ketone. Thus, they can be differentiated.
Therefore, iodoform test can differentiate pairs A and E.

29300.text:
MX is a sparingly soluble salt that follows the given solubility equilibrium at 298 K.
$\mathrm{MX}(\mathrm{s}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{M}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{X}^{-}(\mathrm{aq}) ; \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}}=10^{-10}$
If the standard reduction potential for $\mathrm{M}^{+}(\mathrm{aq}) \xrightarrow{+\mathrm{e}^{-}} \mathrm{M}(\mathrm{s})$ is $\left(\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{M}^{+} / \mathrm{M}}^{\ominus}\right)=0.79 \mathrm{~V}$, then the value of the standard reduction potential for the metal/metal insoluble salt electrode $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{X}^{-} / \mathrm{MX}(\mathrm{s}) / \mathrm{M}}^{\ominus}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ mV. (nearest integer)
[Given : $\frac{2.303 \mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{F}}=0.059 \mathrm{~V}$ ]
29300.sol:
The standard reduction potential for a metal/metal insoluble salt electrode is related to the standard reduction potential of the metal ion and the solubility product $K_{sp}$ of the salt.
The half-cell reaction for the $X^-/MX(s)/M$ electrode is: $MX(s) + e^- \rightarrow M(s) + X^-(aq)$.
This can be viewed as a combination of two processes:
1. $MX(s) \rightleftharpoons M^+(aq) + X^-(aq)$ with equilibrium constant $K_{sp} = 10^{-10}$
2. $M^+(aq) + e^- \rightarrow M(s)$ with $E^\ominus_{M^+/M} = 0.79\text{ V}$
The relation between the standard potentials is given by:
$E^\ominus_{X^-/MX/M} = E^\ominus_{M^+/M} + \frac{2.303RT}{nF} \log_{10} K_{sp}$
Given $n = 1$ and $\frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059\text{ V}$:
$E^\ominus_{X^-/MX/M} = 0.79 + 0.059 \log_{10}(10^{-10})$
$E^\ominus_{X^-/MX/M} = 0.79 + 0.059(-10)$
$E^\ominus_{X^-/MX/M} = 0.79 - 0.59 = 0.20\text{ V}$
To convert the value into mV:
$0.20\text{ V} = 0.20 \times 1000\text{ mV} = 200\text{ mV}$

32173.text: Which of the following statements regarding the energy of the stationary state is true in the following one - electron systems ?
options: $-2.18 \times 10^{-18} \mathrm{ J} \text{ for third orbit of } \mathrm{Li}^{2+} $$\text{ ion }$
$-1.09 \times 10^{-18} \mathrm{ J} \text{ for second orbit of } \mathrm{H} \text{$ atom. }
32173.sol:
The energy of an electron in the $n^{th}$ stationary state of a one-electron system is given by the Bohr's formula:
$E_n = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \frac{Z^2}{n^2}$ J
where $Z$ is the atomic number and $n$ is the principal quantum number.
For option (1): Second orbit of $He^+$ ($Z=2, n=2$)
$E = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \frac{2^2}{2^2} = -2.18 \times 10^{-18}$ J. (Incorrect sign in option)
For option (2): Third orbit of $Li^{2+}$ ($Z=3, n=3$)
$E = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \frac{3^2}{3^2} = -2.18 \times 10^{-18}$ J. (Correct)
For option (3): Second orbit of $H$ atom ($Z=1, n=2$)
$E = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \frac{1^2}{2^2} = -0.545 \times 10^{-18}$ J. (Incorrect value)
For option (4): First orbit of $He^+$ ($Z=2, n=1$)
$E = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \frac{2^2}{1^2} = -8.72 \times 10^{-18}$ J. (Incorrect sign in option)

32340.text:
Which of the following combination of statements is true regarding the interpretation of the atomic orbitals?

$( A )$ An electron in an orbital of high angular momentum stays away from the nucleus than an electron in the orbital of lower angular momentum.

$( B )$ For a given value of the principal quantum number, the size of the orbit is inversely proportional to the azimuthal quantum number.

$( C )$ According to wave mechanics, the ground state angular momentum is equal to $\dfrac{h}{2\pi}$ .

$( D )$ The plot of $ψ$ Vs $r$ for various azimuthal quantum numbers, shows peak shifting towards higher $r$ value.
32340.sol:
Statements (B) and (C) are incorrect.

For a given value of the principal quantum number, the size of the orbit is directly proportional to the azimuthal quantum number and not inversely proportional.
The formula for angular momentum is $\dfrac{h}{2\pi}\sqrt{l( l + 1 )}$
If the electron is in ground state, n will be 1 and the only azimuthal quantum number value can be 0. If l = 0, angular quantum momentum will also be 0. The plot of $ψ$ Vs $r$ for various azimuthal quantum numbers, shows peak shifting towards higher $r$ value.

33388.text: Let the coefficients of the middle terms in the expansion of ${\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}} + \betax\right)}^{4}, {\left(1 - 3\betax\right)}^{2}$ and ${\left(1 - \dfrac{\beta}{2}x\right)}^{6}, \beta > 0$, respectively form the first three terms of an A.P. If $d$ is the common difference of this A.P., then $50 - \dfrac{2d}{{\beta}^{2}}$ is equal to _____ .
33388.sol:
Let the coefficients of the middle terms in the expansion of ${\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}} + \betax\right)}^{4}, {\left(1 - 3\betax\right)}^{2}$ and ${\left(1 - \dfrac{\beta}{2}x\right)}^{6}, \beta > 0$, respectively form the first three terms of an A.P. If $d$ is the common difference of this A.P., then $50 - \dfrac{2d}{{\beta}^{2}}$ is equal to _____ .

Given,

Coefficients of middle terms of given expansions ${\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}} + \betax\right)}^{4}$, ${\left(1 - 3\betax\right)}^{2}$ and ${\left(1 - \dfrac{\beta}{2}x\right)}^{6}$ are $C2 4 \dfrac{1}{6}{\beta}^{2}, C1 2 \left(- 3\beta\right) \text{ and } C3 6 {\left(\dfrac{- \beta}{2}\right)}^{3}$ respectively,

Now it is given that middle terms are forming an $A . P$

So, $2 C1 2 \left(- 3\beta\right) = C3 6 {\left(\dfrac{- \beta}{2}\right)}^{3} + C2 4 \dfrac{1}{6}{\beta}^{2}$

$⇒ 2 . 2\left(- 3\beta\right) = {\beta}^{2} - \dfrac{5{\beta}^{3}}{2}$

$⇒ - 24 = 2\beta - 5{\beta}^{2}$

$⇒ 5{\beta}^{2} - 2\beta - 24 = 0$

$⇒ 5{\beta}^{2} - 12\beta + 10\beta - 24 = 0$

$⇒ \beta\left(5\beta - 12\right) + 2\left(5\beta - 12\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\beta + 2\right)\left(5\beta - 12\right) = 0$

So, $\beta = \dfrac{12}{5}$ and $\beta = - 2$ {which is not possible as $\beta > 0$}

Now $d = C1 2 \left(- 3\beta\right) - C2 4 \dfrac{1}{6}{\beta}^{2} = - 6\beta - {\beta}^{2}$

Now putting the value of $\beta \text{ and } d$ in $50 - \dfrac{2d}{{\beta}^{2}}$ we get,

$50 - \dfrac{2d}{{\beta}^{2}} = 50 - 2\dfrac{\left(- 6\beta - {\beta}^{2}\right)}{{\beta}^{2}} = 50 + \dfrac{12}{\beta} + 2 = 57$

Given,

$X = \left\{z \in C: Re\left(a{z}^{2} + bz\right) = aandRe\left(b{z}^{2} + az\right) = b\right\}$

Now, let $z = x + iy$

So, $Re\left(a{z}^{2} + bz\right) = a$

$⇒ Re\left(a{\left(x + iy\right)}^{2} + b\left(x + iy\right)\right) = a$

$⇒ Re\left(a\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2} + 2ixy\right) + b\left(x + iy\right)\right) = a$

$⇒ a\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right) + bx = a . . . \left(i\right)$

And, $Re\left(b{z}^{2} + az\right) = b$

$⇒ Re\left(b{\left(x + iy\right)}^{2} + a\left(x + iy\right)\right) = b$

$⇒ Re\left(b\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2} + 2ixy\right) + a\left(x + iy\right)\right) = b$

$⇒ b\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right) + ax = b . . . \left(ii\right)$

From $\left(i\right)$ and $\left(ii\right), \left(i\right) - \left(ii\right)$ we get,

$\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right)\left(a - b\right) - x\left(a - b\right) = a - b$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} - x = 1 . . . \left(iii\right)$

From $\left(i\right)$ and $\left(ii\right), \left(i\right) + \left(ii\right)$

$\left(\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right) + x - 1\right)\left(a + b\right) = 0$ (Note: here $a + b \ne 0$ is considered but it is not clear from the question)

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} + x - 1 = 0 . . . \left(iv\right)$

Now from $\left(iii\right)$ and $\left(iv\right)$ we get,

$x = 0, {y}^{2} = - 1$ (No solution)

34046.text:
Let $f: R \to R$ be a function defined as $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}3\left(1 - \dfrac{| x |}{2}\right) & \text{if} & | x | \le 2 \\ 0 & \text{if} & | x | > 2\end{cases}\right .$

Let $g: R \to R$ be given by $g ( x ) = f ( x + 2 ) - f ( x - 2 ) .$ If $n$ and $m$ denote the number of points in $R$ where $g$ is not continuous and not differentiable, respectively, then $n + m$ is equal to ________.
34046.sol:
The given function is $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}3\left(1 - \dfrac{| x |}{2}\right) & if & | x | \le 2 \\ 0 & if & | x | > 2\end{cases}\right)

By using the definition of modulus function, we have $\left|x\right| = \left\{\begin{cases}x, & x \ge 0 \\ - x, & x < 0\end{cases}\right) and also, we know that if $\left|x\right| \le a, ⇒ - a \le x \le a$ and if $\left|x\right| > a, ⇒ x a,$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}3\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{2}\right), & - 2 \le x \le 0 \\ 3\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{2}\right), & 0 xorx > 2\end{cases}\right)

Now, $f\left(x - 2\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}3\left(1 + \dfrac{x - 2}{2}\right), & - 2 \le x - 2 \le 0 \\ 3\left(1 - \dfrac{x - 2}{2}\right), & 0 x - 2orx - 2 > 2\end{cases}\right)

$⇒ f\left(x - 2\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}\dfrac{3x}{2}, & 0 \le x \le 2 \\ 6 - \dfrac{3x}{2}, & 2 xorx > 4\end{cases}\right)

And, $f\left(x + 2\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}3\left(1 + \dfrac{x + 2}{2}\right), & - 2 \le x + 2 \le 0 \\ 3\left(1 - \dfrac{x + 2}{2}\right), & 0 x + 2orx + 2 > 2\end{cases}\right)

$⇒ f\left(x + 2\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}6 + \dfrac{3x}{2}, & - 4 \le x \le - 2 \\ - \dfrac{3x}{2}, & - 2 xorx > 0\end{cases}\right)

Hence, $g\left(x\right) = f\left(x + 2\right) - f\left(x - 2\right) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}\dfrac{3x}{2} + 6, - 4 \le x \le - 2 \\ - \dfrac{3x}{2}, - 2 < x < 2 \\ \dfrac{3x}{2} - 6, 2 \le x \le 4 \\ 0, x \in ( - \infty , - 4 ) ∪ ( 4, \infty )\end{array}\right)

The graph of $g\left(x\right)$ is given below

From the graph we can observe that the function $g\left(x\right)$ is continuous everywhere, hence the number of points where $g\left(x\right)$ is not continuos is $n = 0$ and the graph has sharp corners at the points $\left(- 4, 0\right), \left(4, 0\right), \left(- 2, 3\right) \text{ and } \left(2, - 3\right)$ thus the number of points where $g\left(x\right)$ is not differentiable are $m = 4$

$⇒ n + m = 4 .$

34502.text:
The number of real values of $\lambda$, such that the system of linear equations

$2x - 3y + 5z = 9$

$x + 3y - z = - 18$

$3x - y + \left({\lambda}^{2} - \left|\lambda\right|\right)z = 16$ has no solutions, is
34502.sol:
For the system of linear equations

$2x - 3y + 5z = 9$

$x + 3y - z = - 18$

$3x - y + \left({\lambda}^{2} - \left|\lambda\right|\right)z = 16$ to have no solutions,

$∆$ should be equal to $0$.

i.e. $\Delta = \left|\begin{cases}2 & - 3 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & - 1 \\ 3 & - 1 & {\lambda}^{2} - \left|\lambda\right|\end{cases}\right|$

$= 2\left(3{\lambda}^{2} - 3\left|\lambda\right| - 1\right) + 3\left({\lambda}^{2} - \left|\lambda\right| + 3\right) + 5\left(- 1 - 9\right)$

$= 9{\lambda}^{2} - 9\left|\lambda\right| - 43$

$= 9{\left|\lambda\right|}^{2} - 9\left|\lambda\right| - 43$

Now $∆ = 0$ for $2$ values of $\left|\lambda\right|$ as for the above quadratic the value of determinant is greater than zero.

So, $2$ values of $\lambda$ satisfy the system of equations to obtain no solution.

34728.text: Let $y = y\left(t\right)$ be a solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dt} + \alphay = \gamma{e}^{- \betat}$ Where, $\alpha > 0, \beta > 0$ and $\gamma > 0$. Then ${Lim}_{t \to \infty}y\left(t\right)$
34728.sol:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dt} + \alphay = \gamma \cdot {e}^{- \betat}$

Which is a linear differential equation,

So, integrating factor will be $I . F = {e}^{∫ \alphadt} = {e}^{\alphat}$

So, the solution of differential equation is given by

$y \times {e}^{\alphat} = \gamma ∫ {e}^{- \betat} \times {e}^{\alphat}$

$⇒ y \times {e}^{\alphat} = \gamma ∫ {e}^{\left(\alpha - \beta\right)t}$

$⇒ y \times {e}^{\alphat} = \gamma\dfrac{{e}^{\left(\alpha - \beta\right)t}}{\left(\alpha - \beta\right)} + c$

$⇒ y = \gamma\dfrac{{e}^{- \betat}}{\left(\alpha - \beta\right)} + c{e}^{- \alphat}$

Now finding $\lim_{t \to \infty}y$ we get,

$\lim_{t \to \infty}y = \lim_{t \to \infty}\left(\gamma\dfrac{{e}^{- \betat}}{\left(\alpha - \beta\right)} + c{e}^{- \alphat}\right)$

$⇒ \lim_{t \to \infty}y = \gamma \times 0 + c \times 0 = 0\left\{\text{as}{e}^{- \infty} \to 0\right\}$

35177.text: If the domain of the function $f\left(x\right)$ = {sec}^{- 1}$\left(\dfrac{2x}{5x + 3}\right)$ is $[ \alpha, \beta ) ∪ ( \gamma, \delta ]$, then $\left|3\alpha + 10 \left(\beta + \gamma\right) + 21\delta\right|$ is equal to __________
35177.sol:
We know that,

Domain of ${sec}^{- 1}x$ is $( - \infty , - 1 ] ∪ [ 1, \infty )$.

Now, $f\left(x\right)$ = {sec}^{- 1}$\left(\dfrac{2x}{5x + 3}\right)$

So,

$\dfrac{2x}{5x + 3}$ \le - 1 $\text{or}\dfrac{2x}{5x + 3} \ge 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{2x}{5x + 3} +1 \le 0 \text{or}\dfrac{2x}{5x + 3} -$1 \ge 0$

$⇒ $\dfrac{7x + 3}{5x + 3}$ \le 0 $\text{or}\dfrac{- 3x - 3}{5x + 3} \ge 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{7x + 3}{5x + 3} \le 0 \text{or}\dfrac{x + 1}{5x + 3}$ \le 0$

$⇒ x \in [ - 1, - $\dfrac{3}{5}$ ) ∪ ( - $\dfrac{3}{5}$, - $\dfrac{3}{7}$ ]$

So,

$\alpha = - 1, \beta = - $\dfrac{3}{5}$, \gamma = - $\dfrac{3}{5}$, \delta = - $\dfrac{3}{7}

Now,

\left|3\alpha + 10\left(\beta + \gamma\right) + 21\delta\right| = \left|- 3 - 6 - 6 - 9\right| = 24$

Hence this is the required answer.

Solving $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ $b = \dfrac{6}{5}a = \dfrac{8}{5}$

Normal at $A$ is $\dfrac{\sqrt{5}{a}^{2}x}{8} + \dfrac{5{b}^{2}y}{12} = {a}^{2} + {b}^{2}$

Comparing it $8\sqrt{5}x + \betay = \lambda$

Gives $\lambda = 100, \beta = 15$

So, $\lambda - \beta = 85$

$u = \frac{(2-\sqrt{3}) \pm (2+\sqrt{3})}{2}$, giving $u = 2$ or $u = -\sqrt{3}$ (rejected).

36885.text: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation ${x}^{2} - \sqrt{2}x + \sqrt{6} = 0$ and $\dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}} + 1, \dfrac{1}{{\beta}^{2}} + 1$ be the roots of the equation ${x}^{2} + ax + b = 0$. Then the roots of the equation ${x}^{2} - \left(a + b - 2\right)x + \left(a + b + 2\right) = 0$ are :
options: real and exactly one of them is positive
36885.sol:
Given $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation ${x}^{2} - \sqrt{2}x + \sqrt{6} = 0$

So sum of roots will be $\alpha + \beta = \sqrt{2}$ and product of roots will be $\alpha\beta = \sqrt{6}$

And also given $\dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}} + 1$ and $\dfrac{1}{{\beta}^{2}} + 1$ are roots of ${x}^{2} + ax + b = 0$

So sum of roots will be $- a = \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}} + 1 + \dfrac{1}{{\beta}^{2}} + 1$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{- 1}{{\alpha}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{\beta}^{2}} - 2 . . . . . \left(1\right)$

And similarly product of roots will be,

$b = \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{\beta}^{2}} + 1 + \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}{\beta}^{2}} . . . . \left(2\right)$

Now adding equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ we get,

$a + b = \dfrac{1}{{\left(\alpha\beta\right)}^{2}} - 1 = \dfrac{1}{6} - 1 = - \dfrac{5}{6}$ {as $\alpha\beta = \sqrt{6}$}

Now putting the value of $a + b$ in ${x}^{2} - \left(a + b - 2\right)x + \left(a + b + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - \left(- \dfrac{5}{6} - 2\right)x + \left(2 - \dfrac{5}{6}\right) = 0$

$⇒ 6{x}^{2} + 17x + 7 = 0$

$⇒ x = - \dfrac{7}{3}, x = - \dfrac{1}{2}$ are the roots, both roots are real and negative.

Therefore, Equation of plane when D.R of parallel plane is given is,$\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y + 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{- 6} = \lambda$

$⇒ x = 2\lambda + 1, y = 3\lambda - 2, z = - 6\lambda + 3$

since, $x - y + z = 5$

Thus,

$∴ cos\alpha = 0 + 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

38532.text: Let the vectors $\overset{\to}{{u}_{1}} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{{u}_{2}} = \overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k},$ and $\overset{\to}{{u}_{3}} = c\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ be coplanar. If the vectors $\overset{\to}{{v}_{1}} = \left(a + b\right)\overset{^}{i} + c\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{{v}_{2}} = a\overset{^}{i} + \left(b + c\right)\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}$ and  $\overset{\to}{v}3 = b\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \left(c + a\right)\overset{^}{k}$ are also coplanar, then $6\left(a + b + c\right)$ is equal to
38532.sol:
Given: $\overset{\to}{u}1 = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{u}2 = \overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{u}3 = c\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar.

Also given that,$\overset{\to}{v}1 = \left(a + b\right)\overset{^}{i} + c\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{v}2 = a\overset{^}{i} + \left(b + c\right)\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}$and $\overset{\to}{v}3 = b\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \left(c + a\right)\overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar.

Now, using the condition of coplanar we get,

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & a \\ 1 & b & 1 \\ c & 1 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expanding the determinant along ${R}_{1}$.

$⇒ \left(b - 1\right) - \left(1 - c\right) + a\left(1 - bc\right) = 0$

$⇒ a + b + c = 2 + abc . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Again using the coplanar condition we get,

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a + b & c & c \\ a & b + c & a \\ b & b & c + a\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Apply row transformations, $\left({R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} - \left({R}_{1} + {R}_{2}\right)\right)$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a + b & c & c \\ a & b + c & a \\ - 2a & - 2c & 0\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expand the determinant along ${R}_{1}$.

$⇒ \left(a + b\right)\left(0 + 2ac\right) - c\left(0 + 2{a}^{2}\right) + c\left(- 2ac + 2a\left(b + c\right)\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2{a}^{2}c + 2abc - 2{a}^{2}c - 2a{c}^{2} + 2abc + 2a{c}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ abc = 0$

$∴ a + b + c = 2$ (From eq $\left(i\right)$)

$∴ 6\left(a + b + c\right) = 12$

Hence this is the correct option.

38752.subject: Physics
38752.text: A capacitor $C$ is first charged fully with potential difference of $V_{0}$ and disconnected from the battery. The charged capacitor is connected across an inductor having inductance $L$. In $t \mathrm{~s} \ 25 \%$ of the initial energy in the capacitor is transferred to the inductor. The value of $t$ is $\_\_\_\_$ s.
38752.sol:
In an LC circuit, energy oscillates sinusoidally.
Initial energy in capacitor is $E_0 = \frac{1}{2}CV_0^2$.
When 25% is transferred to the inductor, 75% remains in the capacitor.
Since energy in capacitor varies as $E_C(t) = E_0\cos^2(\omega t)$, we need $\cos^2(\omega t) = 0.75$.
This gives $\sin^2(\omega t) = 0.25$, so $\sin(\omega t) = 0.5$, yielding $\omega t = \frac{\pi}{6}$.
With $\omega = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$, we get $t = \frac{\pi\sqrt{LC}}{6}$ seconds.

38824.text:
For a series $LCR$ circuit, $I$ vs $\omega$ curve is shown

(a) To the left of ${\omega}_{r}$, the circuit is mainly capacitive.
(b) To the left of ${\omega}_{r}$, the circuit is mainly inductive.
(c) At ${\omega}_{r}$, impedance of the circuit is equal to the resistance of the circuit.
(d) At ${\omega}_{r}$, impedance of the circuit is $0$.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
38824.sol:
The impedance of an AC circuit is given by, $Z = \sqrt{{R}^{2} + {\left({X}_{C} - {X}_{L}\right)}^{2}}$.

For current to be maximum $Z$ should be minimum. The value of $Z$ will be minimum when ${X}_{C} - {X}_{L} = 0$. Therefore, the value of $Z = R$. Hence, statement C is correct and statement D is wrong.

To the left of ${\omega}_{r}$ i.e. when $\omega < {\omega}_{r}$, ${X}_{C} > {X}_{L}$. Therefore, the circuit is mainly capacitive. Hence, statement A is correct and statement B is wrong.

41415.text: A short bar magnet placed with its axis at $30^{\circ}$ with an external field of 800 Gauss, experiences a torque of $0.016 \mathrm{~N}. \mathrm{m}$. The work done in moving it from most stable to most unstable position is $\alpha \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~J}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
41415.sol:
For a magnetic dipole in an external field, torque is $\tau = mB\sin\theta$
At 30°: $0.016 = m \times 0.08 \times \sin 30°$
$0.016 = m \times 0.08 \times 0.5$
$m = 0.4$ A·m$^2$
Work done from most stable (aligned, 0°) to most unstable (anti-aligned, 180°) position equals the change in potential energy:
$W = U_0° - U_{180°} = -mB\cos 0° - (-mB\cos 180°) = -mB - mB = 2mB$
$W = 2 \times 0.4 \times 0.08 = 0.064$ J $= 64 \times 10^{-3}$ J
Therefore, $\alpha = 64$

43878.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: If heat is added to a system, its temperature must increase.

Statement II: If positive work is done by a system in a thermodynamic process, its volume must increase.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
43878.sol:
If heat energy is added to a thermodynamic system, one part increases the internal energy and the other part performs some work.

If heat is added to a system, the system can do work without changing its internal energy. Hence, statement 1 is false.

The formula to calculate the work done is given by

$W = ∫ PdV$

From the above equation, it can be concluded that if $W > 0$, i.e., work is done by the system, its volume must increase. Hence, statement II is true.

44194.subject: Physics
44194.text: In a double slit experiment, when one of the slits is covered by a transparent mica sheet of refractive index $1.56$, the central fringe shifts to the position of $7^{th}$ bright fringe, obtained with both slits uncovered. If the light source wavelength is $450$ nm, the thickness of mica sheet is $\alpha \times 10^{-9}$ m. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
44194.sol:
The shift in the central fringe due to the introduction of a transparent sheet of thickness $t$ and refractive index $\mu$ is given by $\Delta y = \dfrac{D}{d}(\mu - 1)t$.

The position of the $n^{th}$ bright fringe is $y_n = n \dfrac{D\lambda}{d}$.

Equating the two, we get:

$\dfrac{D}{d}(\mu - 1)t = n \dfrac{D\lambda}{d}$

$(\mu - 1)t = n\lambda$

Substituting the given values:

$(1.56 - 1)t = 7 \times 450 \times 10^{-9}$

$0.56 t = 3150 \times 10^{-9}$

$t = \dfrac{3150}{0.56} \times 10^{-9}$

$t = 5625 \times 10^{-9}$ m

Comparing with $t = \alpha \times 10^{-9}$ m, we get $\alpha = 5625$.

Answer: $5625$

47426.subject: Chemistry
47426.text: Incorrect statement about $\alpha$-amino acids of proteins among the following is
options: Methionine is an essential amino acid
Zwitterion of valine exhibits amphoteric behaviour
47426.sol:
Methionine is an essential amino acid, so the first statement is correct.

Glycine is the simplest amino acid with the formula $H_2N-CH_2-COOH$. Since its $\alpha$-carbon is attached to two identical hydrogen atoms, it is achiral and does not exhibit enantiomerism. Thus, the second statement is correct.

Glycylalanylglycine is a tripeptide formed by the condensation of three amino acids (glycine, alanine, and glycine). The number of peptide (amide) linkages in a peptide is equal to the number of amino acid residues minus one. Therefore, it has $3 - 1 = 2$ amide linkages, not three. This makes the third statement incorrect.

The zwitterion of an amino acid contains both a basic carboxylate ion ($-COO^-$) and an acidic ammonium ion ($-NH_3^+$), allowing it to react with both acids and bases. Hence, it exhibits amphoteric behaviour, making the fourth statement correct.

Answer: Glycylalanylglycine has three amide linkages

50103.subject: Physics
50103.text:
Consider three point charges $-2Q, Q$ and $-Q$ and three surfaces $S_1, S_2$ and $S_3$ as shown in the figure. Match the entries of List-I with that of List-II.

List-IList-II
(a) Net flux through $S_1$(i) $\dfrac{-2Q}{\varepsilon_0}$
(b) Net flux through $S_2$(ii) $\dfrac{-Q}{\varepsilon_0}$
(c) Net flux through $S_3$(iii) Zero
options: a - ii, b - i, c – iii
a - iii, b - ii, c – i
a - i, b - ii, c – iii
a - ii, b - iii, c – i
50103.sol:
According to Gauss's Law, the net electric flux through any closed surface is given by $\Phi = \dfrac{Q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}$.

For surface $S_1$, the enclosed charges are $-2Q$ and $Q$.
Net charge enclosed by $S_1 = -2Q + Q = -Q$.
Net flux through $S_1 = \dfrac{-Q}{\varepsilon_0}$.
Thus, (a) matches with (ii).

For surface $S_2$, the enclosed charges are $Q$ and $-Q$.
Net charge enclosed by $S_2 = Q + (-Q) = 0$.
Net flux through $S_2 = 0$.
Thus, (b) matches with (iii).

For surface $S_3$, the enclosed charges are $-2Q$, $Q$, and $-Q$.
Net charge enclosed by $S_3 = -2Q + Q + (-Q) = -2Q$.
Net flux through $S_3 = \dfrac{-2Q}{\varepsilon_0}$.
Thus, (c) matches with (i).

The correct matching is a - ii, b - iii, c - i.

Answer: a - ii, b - iii, c – i

50257.subject: Physics
50257.text: Two identical circular current loops carrying equal currents are placed with their axes inclined at $45^\circ$ to each other as shown in the figure. The resultant magnetic field at P is
50257.sol:
The magnetic field at a point on the axis of a circular current loop is given by:

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$

where $R$ is the radius of the loop and $x$ is the distance from the center to the point.

For both loops, the distance from the center to point P is $x = \sqrt{3}R$. Substituting this value:

$B_1 = B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + (\sqrt{3}R)^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + 3R^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(4R^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(8R^3)} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{16R}$

Let the magnetic field due to the first loop be $\vec{B}_1$. Based on the geometry, its axis is along the x-axis, so the field is directed along the positive x-axis:

$\vec{B}_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{16R} \hat{i}$

The second loop is inclined such that its axis makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with the first loop's axis. The magnetic field $\vec{B}_2$ due to this loop is directed along its axis towards P. Resolving this field into components gives:

$\vec{B}_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{16R} (\cos 45^\circ \hat{i} + \sin 45^\circ \hat{j}) = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{16R} \left( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{j} \right)$

The resultant magnetic field at P is the vector sum of the fields from both loops:

$\vec{B}_{net} = \vec{B}_1 + \vec{B}_2$

$\vec{B}_{net} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{16R} \hat{i} + \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{16R} \left( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{j} \right)$

$\vec{B}_{net} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{16R} \left( \left( 1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \right) \hat{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{j} \right)$

$\vec{B}_{net} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{16R} \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{2} + 1}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{j} \right)$

$\vec{B}_{net} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{16\sqrt{2}R} [(\sqrt{2} + 1)\hat{i} + \hat{j}]$

56003.text: The time required for $90\%$ completion of a certain first order reaction is $1$ hour. Calculate the time required for $99.9\%$ completion of the same reaction.
56003.sol:
For a first order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by $k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \left( \dfrac{a}{a-x} \right)

For 90\%$ completion, $t_{90\%} = 1$ hour.

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{1} \log \left( \dfrac{100}{100-90} \right) =2.303 \log 10 = 2.303 \text{ hour}^{-1}

For 99.9\%$ completion, the time required is:

$t_{99.9\%} = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \dfrac{100}{100-99.9} \right)

$ t_{99.9\%} = $\dfrac{2.303}{2.303} \log \left( \dfrac{100}{0.1} \right)

$ t_{99.9\%} = $\log 1000$ = 3$ hours.

Answer: 3$ hours.

57136.subject: Chemistry
57136.text: What is IUPAC name of the following compound ?
57136.sol:
To find the IUPAC name of the given compound, we follow these steps:

1. Identify the principal functional group: The molecule contains a hydroxyl group ($-OH$) and a double bond. The hydroxyl group has higher priority, so it is the principal functional group and must be given the lowest possible locant.

2. Determine the longest carbon chain: The longest continuous carbon chain that contains both the $-OH$ group and the double bond must be selected.
Tracing from the rightmost ethyl group to the leftmost ethyl group gives a chain of 9 carbon atoms. Thus, the parent alkane is nonane.

3. Number the chain: We number the chain to give the principal functional group ($-OH$) the lowest possible number.
Numbering from right to left:
C1, C2: Ethyl group on the right ($-CH_2-CH_3$)
C3: Carbon with a methyl substituent
C4: Carbon with the $-OH$ group
C5, C6: Carbons of the double bond
C7: Carbon with a methyl substituent
C8, C9: Ethyl group on the left ($-CH_2-CH_3$)
In this numbering, the $-OH$ group is at position 4.
If we numbered from left to right, the $-OH$ group would be at position 6. Therefore, the right-to-left numbering is correct.

4. Identify substituents and their positions:
- A methyl group at C-3.
- A methyl group at C-7.
- A double bond starting at C-5.
- The hydroxyl group at C-4.

5. Assemble the name:
Combining these parts, we get: 3,7-dimethyl + non + 5-en + 4-ol $\rightarrow$ 3,7-dimethylnon-5-en-4-ol.

Answer: 3,7-Dimethylnon-5-en-4-ol

60231.text: The area of the triangle formed by the co-ordinate axes and a tangent to the curve $x \mathrm{y}=a^2$ at the point $\left(x_1, \mathrm{y}_1\right)$ is ________ sq.units (where $a, x_1 and y_1$ are non zero)
60231.sol:
The tangent to the curve $xy = a^2$ at point $(x_1, y_1)$ has equation $y_1x + x_1y = 2a^2$, derived from differentiating $xy = a^2$ to obtain $\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{y}{x}$ and using point-slope form.

The x-intercept occurs at $\left(\frac{2a^2}{y_1}, 0\right)$ and the y-intercept at $\left(0, \frac{2a^2}{x_1}\right)$, found by setting $y = 0 and x = 0$ respectively in the tangent equation.

The area of the triangle formed by the coordinate axes and this tangent is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot \left|\frac{2a^2}{y_1}\right| \cdot \left|\frac{2a^2}{x_1}\right| = \frac{4a^4}{2|x_1y_1|}$.

Since $x_1y_1 = a^2 \gt 0$, the area simplifies to $\frac{2a^4}{a^2} = 2a^2$.

Final answer: $2a^2$

60267.sol:
The derivative of $f(x) = x \cdot e^{x-x^2}$ is found using the product rule, with $u(x) = x and v(x) = e^{x-x^2}$.

Since $u'(x) = 1 and v'(x) = e^{x-x^2}(1-2x)$ by the chain rule, we obtain the derivative:

$f'(x) = e^{x-x^2} + x e^{x-x^2}(1-2x) = e^{x-x^2}(1 + x - 2x^2) = -e^{x-x^2}(2x^2 - x - 1)$.

The exponential term $e^{x-x^2}$ is always positive, so the sign of $f'(x)$ depends on $-(2x^2 - x - 1)$.

Solving $2x^2 - x - 1 = 0$ gives $x = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{1+8}}{4} = \frac{1 \pm 3}{4}$, yielding roots at $x = -\frac{1}{2}$ and x = 1.

For $f'(x) \gt 0$, we require $2x^2 - x - 1 \lt 0$, which occurs between the roots: $-\frac{1}{2} \lt x \lt 1$.

Therefore, the function is increasing on $\left(-\frac{1}{2}, 1\right)$, corresponding to option B.

60567.text: The area of the region enclosed by the lines $y = 2x, 2y = x$ and $x = 2$ (in sq.units) is...
60567.sol:
The given lines are $y = 2x$, $y = \dfrac{x}{2}$, and $x = 2$.

The points of intersection of the lines are $(0,0)$, $(2,4)$, and $(2,1)$.

The region is bounded by the upper line $y = 2x$ and the lower line $y = \dfrac{x}{2}$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$.

The area of the region is given by the integral of the difference between the upper and lower curves:

$\text{Area} = \int_{0}^{2} \left(2x - \dfrac{x}{2}\right) dx$

$\text{Area} = \int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{3x}{2} dx$

$\text{Area} = \left[ \dfrac{3x^2}{4} \right]_{0}^{2}$

$\text{Area} = \dfrac{3(2)^2}{4} - 0 = 3$

Answer: $3$

60732.text: Let the circle with centre at origin pass through the vertices of an equilateral triangle $A B C$. If $A \equiv(2,4)$, then the length of the median through A is
60732.sol:
Given the circle centered at $O(0,0)$ passes through the vertices of equilateral triangle ABC, with vertex $A$ at $(2,4)$.

For an equilateral triangle, the centroid $G$ coincides with the circumcenter, hence $G = (0,0)$.

The centroid divides the median $AM$ in the ratio $2:1$, so $AG = \frac{2}{3} AM$. The distance between $A(2,4)$ and $G(0,0)$ is $AG = \sqrt{(2-0)^2 + (4-0)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 16} = \sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}$.

Substituting into the centroid relation, $2\sqrt{5} = \frac{2}{3} AM$, so $AM = \frac{3}{2} \cdot 2\sqrt{5} = 3\sqrt{5}$.

Thus, the length of the median through $A$ is $3\sqrt{5}$ units, corresponding to option B.

63499.subject: Mathematics
63499.text: 21 friends were invited for a party. Two round tables can accommodate 12 and 9 friends each. The number of ways of the seating arrangements of friends is.....
63499.sol:
The arrangement involves partitioning the 21 friends into groups of 12 and 9, then arranging them at round tables where only relative order matters.

The number of ways to select 12 friends for the first table is $\binom{21}{12} = \frac{21!}{12!9!}$, with the remaining 9 assigned to the second table.

For each table with $n$ persons, circular permutations yield $(n-1)!$ distinct arrangements: $11!$ for the first table and $8!$ for the second.

Multiplying the selection and arrangement counts gives $\frac{21!}{12!9!} \cdot 11! \cdot 8!$.

Simplifying, since $12! = 12 \times 11!$ and $9! = 9 \times 8!$, we substitute to get $\frac{21!}{(12 \cdot 11!)(9 \cdot 8!)} \cdot 11! \cdot 8! = \frac{21!}{12 \cdot 9} = \frac{21!}{108}$.

Reducing the fraction $\frac{21!}{108}$ by the greatest common divisor (12) gives $\frac{35 \cdot 19!}{9}$, matching option C.

63984.text: In a triangle ABC with usual notations if, $\cot \frac{A}{2}=\frac{b+c}{a}$, then the triangle $A B C$ is
63984.sol:
Given the condition in triangle ABC: $\cot \frac{A}{2} = \frac{b + c}{a}$.

Using the Law of Sines, $a = 2R \sin A$, $b = 2R \sin B$, $c = 2R \sin C$, substitute into the equation:

$\cot \frac{A}{2} = \frac{\sin B + \sin C}{\sin A}$.

Apply sum-to-product and double-angle identities:

$\sin B + \sin C = 2 \sin \left(\frac{B + C}{2}\right) \cos\left(\frac{B - C}{2}\right)
and \sin A = 2 \sin \frac{A}{2} \cos \frac{A}{2}.

From the angle sum $ A + B + C = $\pi, note that \frac{B + C}{2} = \frac{\pi - A}{2} = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{A}{2},
so \sin \left(\frac{B + C}{2}\right) = \cos \frac{A}{2}.

Substitute and simplify:

$\cot $\frac{A}{2} = \frac{2 \cos \frac{A}{2} \cos \left(\frac{B - C}{2}\right)}{2 \sin \frac{A}{2} \cos \frac{A}{2}} = \frac{\cos \left(\frac{B - C}{2}\right)}{\sin \frac{A}{2}}.

Since $\cot $\frac{A}{2} = \frac{\cos \frac{A}{2}}{\sin \frac{A}{2}}, equate:

\cos \frac{A}{2} = \cos \left(\frac{B - C}{2}\right).$

Given the domain constraints, $\frac{A}{2} = \pm \frac{B - C}{2},$ leading to $A = B - C$ or $A = C - B$.

Substitute into $A + B + C = \pi$:
For $A = B - C$, $B - C + B + C = \pi \impliesB = \frac{\pi}{2}.$
For $A = C - B$, $C - B + B + C = \pi \impliesC = \frac{\pi}{2}.$

In both cases, triangle ABC is right-angled.

The correct choice is $\boxed{C}$.

65579.text:
In an a.c. circuit containing L, C and R in series, the ratio of apparent power to the true power is
(Z= impedance of the circuit and R= resistance )
65579.sol:
Apparent power is given by $P_{app} = V_{rms} I_{rms}$

True power is given by $P_{true} = V_{rms} I_{rms} \cos \phi$

The ratio of apparent power to true power is $\dfrac{P_{app}}{P_{true}} = \dfrac{V_{rms} I_{rms}}{V_{rms} I_{rms} \cos \phi} = \dfrac{1}{\cos \phi}$

In a series LCR circuit, the power factor is $\cos \phi = \dfrac{R}{Z}$

Substituting this value, the ratio becomes $\dfrac{Z}{R}$

Answer: $\dfrac{Z}{R}$

66556.subject: Physics
66556.text: A photon and an electron have equal energy E. The ratio of $\lambda$(electron) to $\lambda$(photon) is proportional to
66556.sol:
For a photon of energy $E$, the wavelength is given by $\lambda_{photon} = \dfrac{hc}{E}$.

For an electron of kinetic energy $E$, the momentum is $p = \sqrt{2mE}$. The de Broglie wavelength of the electron is $\lambda_{electron} = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}$.

Taking the ratio of the wavelength of the electron to that of the photon, we get:

$\dfrac{\lambda_{electron}}{\lambda_{photon}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}}{\dfrac{hc}{E}} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}} \times \dfrac{E}{hc} = \dfrac{\sqrt{E}}{c\sqrt{2m}}$

Since $h$, $c$, and $m$ are constants, the ratio is directly proportional to $\sqrt{E}$.

$\dfrac{\lambda_{electron}}{\lambda_{photon}} \propto \sqrt{E}$

Thus, the ratio is proportional to $\sqrt{E} : 1$.

Answer: $\sqrt{E} : 1$

69476.text: In the following combination of logic gates, the output $Y$ can be written in the terms of inputs A and B as
69476.sol:
Circuit output analysis: The circuit contains two AND gates, one OR gate, and two NOT gates arranged in parallel branches feeding the final OR gate.

The top branch processes inputs through an AND gate followed by a NOT gate, producing the term $\overline{A \cdot B}$.

The bottom branch processes input $B$ through a NOT gate before combining with $A$ in an AND gate, yielding $A \cdot \overline{B}$.

The final output $Y$ is the OR combination of these branch outputs: $Y = (\overline{A \cdot B}) + (A \cdot \overline{B})$.

This expression corresponds to option D.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

69981.subject: Physics
69981.text: A monoatomic ideal gas, initially at temperature $T_1$ is enclosed in a cylinder fitted with frictionless piston. The gas is allowed to expand adiabatically to a temperature $\mathrm{T}_2$ by releasing the piston suddenly. $L_1$ and $L_2$ are the lengths of the gas columns before and after the expansion respectively. The ratio $T_2 / T_1$ is
69981.sol:
For an adiabatic process
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{T}_1 \mathrm{ V}_1^{\gamma-1}=\mathrm{T}_2 \mathrm{ V}_2^{\gamma-1} \\
\therefore \quad & \frac{\mathrm{ T}_2}{\mathrm{ T}_1}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}_1}{\mathrm{ V}_2}\right)^{\gamma-1}
\end{aligned}$
For a monoatomic gas, $\gamma=\frac{5}{3}\begin{array}{ll} & \Rightarrow \gamma-1=\frac{5}{3}-1=\frac{2}{3} \\
& \text{Volume }=\text{ Area } \times \text{ Length, } \\
\therefore \quad & \mathrm{V}_1=\mathrm{AL}_1 \text{ and } \mathrm{V}_2=\mathrm{AL}_2 \\
\therefore \quad & \frac{\mathrm{ T}_2}{\mathrm{ T}_1}=\left[\frac{\mathrm{AL}_1}{\mathrm{AL}]_2}\right]^{2 / 3}=\left[\frac{\mathrm{L}_1}{\mathrm{ L}_2}\right]^{2 / 3} \\
\therefore \quad & \frac{\mathrm{ T}_2}{\mathrm{ T}_1}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{L}_1}{\mathrm{ L}_2}\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}
\end{array}$

70197.subject: Physics
70197.text: In a single slit diffraction pattern, identify the incorrect statement from the following.
options: The fringes have unequal width and unequal intensity.
The fringes have equal width and equal intensity.
70197.sol:
Single-slit diffraction produces a pattern where light waves bend around obstacles or spread after passing through a narrow aperture. The central maximum has angular width $2\lambda/a$, while secondary maxima each have width $\lambda/a$, establishing unequal fringe widths.

Intensity distribution shows the central maximum as brightest, with secondary maxima intensities decreasing rapidly—the first secondary maximum is approximately $4.5\%$ of the central intensity. This confirms unequal intensities.

Option D claims fringes have equal width and equal intensity, which contradicts the fundamental properties of single-slit diffraction. This pattern distinctly features both unequal widths and unequal intensities.

The incorrect statement is $\boxed{D}$.

71036.subject: Biology
71036.text: The saprotrophs are most essential in ________ food chain.
71036.sol:
Saprotrophs are organisms that obtain their nutrition from dead and decaying organic matter. They play a primary and essential role in the detritus food chain, which begins with dead organic material (detritus) rather than living plants.

In this food chain, saprotrophs (such as fungi and bacteria) break down complex organic matter into simpler inorganic substances, recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.

Answer: detritus

71312.subject: Biology
71312.text: Application of which plant hormone overcomes the requirement of vernalization?
71312.sol:
Vernalization is the process of inducing flowering in plants by exposing them to prolonged cold temperatures.

In certain plants, especially biennials such as cabbage and carrots, the requirement for cold treatment can be replaced by the application of gibberellins.

Gibberellins stimulate stem elongation (bolting) and induce flowering, thereby overcoming the need for vernalization.

Answer: Gibberellins

71323.subject: Biology
71323.text: If the dark period is interrupted even by a flash of light, plants like tobacco and soybean ______
options: cannot be made to flower again.
71323.sol:
Tobacco and soybean are short-day plants.

Short-day plants require a continuous and uninterrupted dark period exceeding a critical duration to initiate flowering.

If the dark period is interrupted even by a brief flash of light, the phytochrome system is reset, which inhibits the flowering process.

Therefore, these plants will not flower.

Answer: will not flower.

71354.subject: Biology
71354.text: In a typical monohybrid, a cross with respect to a certain trait, 120 plants are obtained in the $F_2$ generation. What will be the approximate number of homozygous and heterozygous plants respectively?
71354.sol:
In a typical monohybrid cross, the $F_2$ generation genotypic ratio is $1 : 2 : 1$ for homozygous dominant, heterozygous, and homozygous recessive respectively.

The proportion of homozygous plants (both dominant and recessive) is $\dfrac{1 + 1}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

The proportion of heterozygous plants is $\dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Given the total number of plants in the $F_2$ generation is $120$.

Number of homozygous plants = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times 120 = 60$.

Number of heterozygous plants = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times 120 = 60$.

Answer: 60 and 60.

71452.subject: Biology
71452.text: The formation of ATP by oxidative phosphorylation takes place in ____.
71452.sol:
Oxidative phosphorylation is the process in which ATP is formed as a result of the transfer of electrons from NADH or FADH_2$ to O_2$ by a series of electron carriers. This process takes place in the Electron Transport System (ETS) located in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

In glycolysis and the Krebs cycle, ATP is formed through substrate-level phosphorylation.

Fermentation is an anaerobic process that does not involve oxidative phosphorylation.

Answer: ETS

71500.sol:
Unisexuality is the condition where flowers are either male or female. Mulberry is an example of a plant with unisexual flowers.

Protandry is a condition where the anthers mature earlier than the stigma of the same flower. Disc florets of sunflower exhibit protandry.

Protogyny is a condition where the stigma matures earlier than the anthers. Gloriosa is an example of a plant exhibiting protogyny.

Prepotency is the phenomenon where pollen from a different flower germinates faster on the stigma than pollen from the same flower. Apple is an example of prepotency.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III).

71852.subject: Chemistry
71852.text: Which of the following alkenes forms formaldehyde and acetaldehyde on ozonolysis?
71852.sol:
Ozonolysis of an alkene involves the cleavage of the carbon-carbon double bond to form carbonyl compounds.

To find the original alkene, we remove the oxygen atoms from the carbonyl products and join the carbon atoms with a double bond.

The given products are formaldehyde (HCHO$) and acetaldehyde (CH_3CHO$).

Joining the carbonyl carbons of $HCHO$ and $CH_3CHO$ gives $CH_3-CH=CH_2$, which is propene.

Reaction:
$CH_3-CH=CH_2 \xrightarrow{O_3, Zn/H_2O} CH_3CHO + HCHO$

Thus, propene forms formaldehyde and acetaldehyde on ozonolysis.

Answer: Propene

72195.subject: Physics
72195.text: Two coils P and Q are kept near each other. When no current flows through coil P and currrent in coil Q increases at the rate of 10 A/s, the e.m.f. in coil P is 12 mV. When coil Q carries no current and current 1.5 A flows through coil P, the magnetic flux linked with the coil Q is
72195.sol:
The induced e.m.f. in coil P due to the rate of change of current in coil Q is given by

$e_P = M \dfrac{di_Q}{dt}$

Substituting the given values,

$12 \times 10^{-3} = M \times 10$

$M = 1.2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ H}$

The magnetic flux linked with coil Q when current $i_P$ flows through coil P is

$\phi_Q = M i_P$

$\phi_Q = (1.2 \times 10^{-3}) \times 1.5$

$\phi_Q = 1.8 \times 10^{-3} \text{ Wb} = 1.8 \text{ mWb}$

Answer: $1.8 \text{ mWb}$

72286.subject: Physics
72286.text: A rod has mass $(4 \pm 0.01)$ kg, radius $(2 \pm 0.02)$ cm and length $(50 \pm 0.05)$ cm. The maximum percentage error in the measurement of density is
72286.sol:
Density of the rod is given by $\rho = \dfrac{M}{V} = \dfrac{M}{\pi r^2 L}$

The maximum percentage error in density is

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = \left( \dfrac{\Delta M}{M} + 2 \dfrac{\Delta r}{r} + \dfrac{\Delta L}{L} \right) \times 100$

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = \left( \dfrac{0.01}{4} + 2 \times \dfrac{0.02}{2} + \dfrac{0.05}{50} \right) \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = (0.0025 + 0.02 + 0.001) \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = 0.0235 \times 100 = 2.35\ \%$

Answer: $2.35\ \%$

72287.subject: Physics
72287.text: The metre scale is used to measure the volume of a block. The measured length is $10$ cm, breadth is $20$ cm and height is $25$ cm. The percentage error in the measurement of volume of a block is… (least count of metre scale $= 1$mm)
72287.sol:
The volume of the block is given by $V = L \times B \times H$

The maximum relative error in the measurement of volume is

$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} = \dfrac{\Delta L}{L} + \dfrac{\Delta B}{B} + \dfrac{\Delta H}{H}$

Given $L = 10$ cm, $B = 20$ cm, $H = 25$ cm and the least count of the metre scale is $\Delta L = \Delta B = \Delta H = 1$ mm $= 0.1$ cm.

Substituting the values:

$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} = \dfrac{0.1}{10} + \dfrac{0.1}{20} + \dfrac{0.1}{25}$

$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} = 0.01 + 0.005 + 0.004 = 0.019$

The percentage error in volume is $\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = 0.019 \times 100 = 1.9\%$

Answer: $1.9\ \%$

73819.subject: General Ability
73819.text: Which one of the following findings is NOT observed in Rutherford's Nuclear Model of Atom?
options: There is a neutral centre in an atom called nucleus
Nearly all the mass of an atom resides in the nucleus
The electrons revolve around the nucleus in a circular path
The size of a nucleus is very small as compared to the size of atom
73819.sol:
According to Rutherford's Nuclear Model of Atom, the positive charge and most of the mass of the atom are densely concentrated in an extremely small region called the nucleus. The nucleus is positively charged, not neutral.

The other statements are correct postulates of Rutherford's model:
Nearly all the mass of an atom resides in the nucleus.
The electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular paths called orbits.
The size of the nucleus is very small as compared to the size of the atom.

Therefore, the statement that there is a neutral centre in an atom called nucleus is not observed in Rutherford's model.

Answer: There is a neutral centre in an atom called nucleus

74117.subject: General Ability
options: conservation of energy and non-conservation of charge.
conservation of charge and non-conversation of linear momentum.
conservation of charge and non-conservation of energy.
conservation of energy, momentum and charge.
74117.sol:
Conservation laws are fundamental to our understanding of the physical world, in that they describe which processes can or cannot occur in nature. For example, the conservation law of energy states that the total quantity of energy in an isolated system does not change, though it may change form. With respect to classical physics, conservation laws include conservation of energy, mass (or matter), linear momentum, angular momentum, and electric charge.
Conservation laws have broad application in physics, as well as in other fields such as chemistry, biology, geology, and engineering.

Given that $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{2+x^2}{1+x}-A x-B\right)=3$.

$\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{2+\mathrm{x}^2}{1+\mathrm{x}}-\mathrm{Ax}-\mathrm{B}\right)=3 \\
\Rightarrow & \lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{2+\mathrm{x}^2-\mathrm{Ax}-\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{Ax}^2-\mathrm{Bx}}{1+\mathrm{x}}\right)=3 \\
\Rightarrow & \lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty}\left[\frac{(1-\mathrm{A}) \mathrm{x}^2-(\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}) \mathrm{x}+2-\mathrm{B}}{1+\mathrm{x}}\right]=3
\end{aligned}$
Applying L'Hospital rule,
$2 x(1-A)-(A+B)=3$
Comparing coefficients
$\begin{array}{ll} & 2(1-A)=0 \\
\therefore \quad & A=1 \text{ and } \\
& -(A+B)=3 \\
\therefore \quad & B=-3-1=-4 \\
& A+B=-3 \\
& A=1 . B=-4
\end{array}$

78752.subject: Mathematics
78752.text:
Passage: $P(-2,-3,5)$, $Q(4,-1,5)$, $R(6,-4,8)$ and $S(2,-6,10)$ are four points.

Question: Consider the following statements :
I. $PQ$ is parallel to $RS$.
II. $PR$ is perpendicular to $QS$.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
78752.sol:
The direction ratios of the line segment $PQ$ are $4 - (-2), -1 - (-3), 5 - 5$, which gives $\langle 6, 2, 0 \rangle$.

The direction ratios of the line segment $RS$ are $2 - 6, -6 - (-4), 10 - 8$, which gives $\langle -4, -2, 2 \rangle$.

Since the ratios of their corresponding direction ratios are not equal ($\dfrac{6}{-4} \neq \dfrac{2}{-2} \neq \dfrac{0}{2}$), $PQ$ is not parallel to $RS$. Thus, Statement I is incorrect.

The direction ratios of the line segment $PR$ are $6 - (-2), -4 - (-3), 8 - 5$, which gives $\langle 8, -1, 3 \rangle$.

The direction ratios of the line segment $QS$ are $2 - 4, -6 - (-1), 10 - 5$, which gives $\langle -2, -5, 5 \rangle$.

For $PR$ to be perpendicular to $QS$, the dot product of their direction vectors must be zero. Calculating the dot product:

$\vec{PR} \cdot \vec{QS} = (8)(-2) + (-1)(-5) + (3)(5) = -16 + 5 + 15 = 4$

Since the dot product is not zero, $PR$ is not perpendicular to $QS$. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

Therefore, neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct.

Answer: Neither I nor II

79235.subject: Mathematics
79235.text: What is the area of the parallelogram whose sides are represented by the vectors $\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ and $2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$?
79235.sol:
Let $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$.

The area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is given by $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$.

$\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 3 \\ 2 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 2 \end{vmatrix}$

$= \hat{i}(4 - 3) - \hat{j}(2 - 6) + \hat{k}(1 - 4)$

$= \hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$

The magnitude of the cross product is:

$|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 4^2 + (-3)^2}$

$= \sqrt{1 + 16 + 9} = \sqrt{26}$

The area of the parallelogram is $\sqrt{26} square units.

Answer: \sqrt{26}$ square units

Arrange the following in the correct development sequence related to microsporogenesis :
A. Microspore tetrads
B. Sporogenous tissue
C. Pollen grains
D. Pollen mother cells
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
80456.sol:
During the development of an anther, the cells of the sporogenous tissue undergo meiotic divisions to form microspore tetrads. Each cell of the sporogenous tissue acts as a pollen mother cell (PMC). The PMCs undergo meiosis to form microspore tetrads. As the anthers mature and dehydrate, the microspores dissociate from each other and develop into pollen grains.

The correct developmental sequence is:
Sporogenous tissue $\rightarrow$ Pollen mother cells $\rightarrow$ Microspore tetrads $\rightarrow$ Pollen grains.

This corresponds to the sequence B, D, A, C.

Answer: B, D, A, C

80555.subject: Botany
80555.text: Which one of the following pairs of plant structures has haploid number of chromosomes?
options: Megaspore mother cell and antipodal cells
80555.sol:
In angiosperms a single diploid megaspore mother cell matures within an ovule. Through meiosis it gives rise to four megaspores (haploid). In most plants only one of these megaspores survive. This functional megaspore divides three times by mitosis and produces eight haploid nuclei enclosed within a 7-celled embryo sac. One nucleus is located near the opening of embryo sac in egg cell. Two nuclei are located in a single cell in the midde of embryo sac and are called polar nuclei, two nuclei are contained in cells called synergids that flank the egg cell and other three nuclei are resided in the cells called antipodals, located at the end of embryo sac, opposite the egg cell.
Nucellus is centrally located mass of thin-walled parenchymatous cells covered by integuments in ovule.

84955.text: PCR and Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism are the methods for
84955.sol:
The hypervariable regions of DNA have Variable Number of Tandem repeats (VNTRs) of short nucleotide sequences which are specific for each individual (except for monozygotic twins). Variations also occur due to mutations, small deletions or insertions. Therefore, DNA cut by a particular endonuclease will have different lengths in different persons. This phenomenon is called Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism. It is the basis of genetic (or DNA) fingerprinting and is useful in identifying individuals from their semen, blood or tissues or any other DNA sample and resolution of parent hood disputes.
Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is also useful in genetic fingerprinting as it can amplify the DNA sample even if available in a very small amount.

92593.text: An ${He}^{+}$ ion in the excited state, on the transition to the ground state, emits two photons in succession with wavelengths $108 . 5$ and $30 . 4nm$. What is the quantum number $n$ corresponding to the excited state of ${He}^{+}$ ion.
92593.sol:
The value of $hc = 1242nmeV$

∴ The energy of the first photon is

$\Delta {E ⁡}_{1} = \dfrac{\text{hc}}{{\lambda}_{1}} = \dfrac{1 2 4 2 n \text{m} \text{eV}}{1 0 8 \text{.} 5 n \text{m}} = 1 1 \text{.} 4 5 \text{eV}$

The energy of the second photon is

$\Delta {E ⁡}_{2} = \dfrac{\text{hc}}{{\lambda}_{2}} = \dfrac{1 2 4 2 n \text{m} \text{eV}}{3 0 \text{.} 4 n \text{m}} = 4 0 \text{.} 8 6 \text{eV}$

The total energy emitted by the electron during jumping from n2 to n1 is $\DeltaE = \Delta{E}_{1} + \Delta{E}_{2}$
$= ( 11 . 45 + 40 . 86 ) eV = 52 . 31eV$

or $\Delta E ⁡ = 1 3 \text{.} 6 {Z ⁡}^{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{{n}_{1}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{n}_{2}^{2}}\right) \text{eV}$

or $\Delta E ⁡ = 1 3 \text{.} 6 {Z ⁡}^{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{{n}_{1}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{n}_{}^{2}}\right) \text{eV}$

or $5 2 \text{.} 3 1 \text{eV} = 1 3 \text{.} 6 {Z ⁡}^{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{{n}_{1}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{n}_{}^{2}}\right) \text{eV}$

But the final state of the electron is the ground state

∴ ${n}_{1} = 1$

∴ $5 2 \text{.} 3 1 \text{eV} = 1 3 \text{.} 6 {Z ⁡}^{2} \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}\right) \text{eV}$

or $\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}\right) {\text{Z}}^{2} = \dfrac{5 2 \text{.} 3 1}{1 3 \text{.} 6}$

or $\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}\right) {\text{Z}}^{2} = 3 \text{.} 8 5$

or $1 - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}} = \dfrac{3 \text{.} 8 5}{{2}^{2}} = \dfrac{3 \text{.} 8 5}{4} = 0 \text{.} 9 6 \left({\text{For He}}^{+} \text{Z} = 2\right)$

∴ $\dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}} = 1 - 0 \text{.} 9 6 = 0 \text{.} 0 4$

or ${n}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{0 \text{.} 0 4} = 2 5$

∴ $n = 5$

Here $\dfrac{dN ( t )}{dt}$ is the rate of radioactive decay at time $t$. If the number of radioactive nuclei of this element decreases by a factor of $p$ after $4 . 16yr$, the value of$p$ is
93994.sol:
$\left|\dfrac{dN}{dt}\right|$= |Activity of radioactive substance|

$= \lambdaN = \lambda{N}_{0}e^{- \lambdat} ( ∵ N = {N}_{0}e^{- \lambdat} )$

Taking log both sides

$ln\left|\dfrac{dN}{dt}\right| = ln ( \lambda{N}_{0} ) - \lambdat$

Hence, ln$\left|\dfrac{dN}{dt}\right|$~versus& $t$ graph is a straight line with slope-$\lambda$.

From the graph, we can see that,

$\lambda = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5{yr}^{- 1}$

Now applying the equation

$N = {N}_{0}e^{- \lambdat} = {N}_{0}e^{- 0.5 \times 4.16}$

$= {N}_{0}e^{- 2.08} = {N}_{0}e^{- 2 \times \left(0 . 693\right)} = 0.125{N}_{0}$

$= \dfrac{{N}_{0}}{8}$

i.e. nuclei decrease by a factor of $8$.

Hence the answer is $8$.

101183.subject: Physics
101183.text: A medical centrifuge starting from rest is accelerated at a constant uniform rate of $5\pi \text{ rad s}^{-2}$. The time taken by the centrifuge to reach a rotational speed of $3000 \text{ rpm}$ is:
101183.sol:
Given, initial angular speed $\omega_0 = 0$
Angular acceleration $\alpha = 5\pi \text{ rad s}^{-2}$
Final angular speed $\omega = 3000 \text{ rpm}$

First, convert the final angular speed into $\text{rad s}^{-1}$:
$\omega = 3000 \times \dfrac{2\pi}{60} \text{ rad s}^{-1} = 100\pi \text{ rad s}^{-1}$

Using the first equation of rotational kinematics:
$\omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t$
$100\pi = 0 + (5\pi) t$
$t = \dfrac{100\pi}{5\pi} = 20 \text{ s}$

Answer: $20 \text{ s}$

A source of sound emits sound waves at frequency $f_0$. It is moving towards an observer with fixed speed $v_s\left(v_s < v\right.$, where $v$ is the speed of sound in air.) 102542.sol:
According to Doppler's effect, the apparent frequency of sound when both source and observer are moving towards each other

\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow$& f=\frac{\left(v+v_0\right) f_0}{ \left(v-v_0\right)}\\
\Rightarrow & f=\left(\frac{v}{v-v_s}\right)f_0+\left(\frac{v_0}{v-v_s}\right)f_0
\end{array}

\Rightarrow \quad f=\left(\frac{f_0}{v-v_s}\right)v_0+\left(\frac{f_0}{v-v_s}\right)v

Equation of straight line, $ y=m x+c$ which is equation of straight line making an intercept $c$ on $Y$-axis, Slope of the graph =\frac{f_0}{v-v_s} and intercept =\frac{v f_0{ }^{{}^{\circ}}}{v-v_s} This condition is represented in graph A plotted between $ f$ and $v_0$.
Hence, option (c) is correct.$

103308.subject: Physics
103308.text: Two resistors, one having a positive temperature coefficient of resistance ($+\alpha$) and the other having a negative temperature coefficient of resistance ($-\alpha$), have the same resistance $R_0$ at an initial temperature. They are connected in parallel across an ideal battery of constant voltage $V$. If the temperature of the entire setup is uniformly increased, how will the total power dissipated by the circuit and the power dissipated by the resistor with the positive temperature coefficient ($+\alpha$) change?
options: Total power remains constant, power of the $+\alpha$ resistor decreases
Total power decreases, power of the $+\alpha$ resistor increases
Total power increases, power of the $+\alpha$ resistor decreases
Both total power and power of the $+\alpha$ resistor increase
103308.sol:
Let the change in temperature be $\Delta T$.

The resistance of the two resistors at the new temperature will be $R_1 = R_0(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$ and $R_2 = R_0(1 - \alpha \Delta T)$.

Since they are connected in parallel, the equivalent resistance of the circuit is:
$R_{eq} = \dfrac{R_1 R_2}{R_1 + R_2} = \dfrac{R_0^2(1 - \alpha^2 \Delta T^2)}{2R_0} = \dfrac{R_0}{2}(1 - \alpha^2 \Delta T^2)$

As temperature increases, $\Delta T$ increases, so $(1 - \alpha^2 \Delta T^2)$ decreases. Thus, the equivalent resistance $R_{eq}$ decreases.

The total power dissipated by the circuit is $P_{total} = \dfrac{V^2}{R_{eq}}$. Since $V$ is constant and $R_{eq}$ decreases, the total power increases.

For the resistor with the positive temperature coefficient ($+\alpha$), its resistance $R_1 = R_0(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$ increases with temperature.

The power dissipated by this individual resistor is $P_1 = \dfrac{V^2}{R_1}$. Since $V$ is constant and $R_1$ increases, the power $P_1$ decreases.

Therefore, the total power increases while the power of the $+\alpha$ resistor decreases.

Answer: Total power increases, power of the $+\alpha$ resistor decreases

103321.text: An infinite ladder network is constructed with identical series resistors of unknown value $R$ on both the top and bottom branches, and identical shunt resistors of $20 \Omega$ connecting the branches. If the equivalent resistance of this entire infinite network measured across the input terminals is $5 \Omega$, what is the value of the individual series resistor $R$?
103321.sol:
Let the equivalent resistance of the infinite network be $R_{eq}$.

Since the network is infinite, removing one repeating unit leaves the equivalent resistance unchanged.

The repeating unit consists of two series resistors $R$ (one on the top branch, one on the bottom) and one shunt resistor of $20 \Omega$.

The equivalent resistance can be written as:
$R_{eq} = R + R + \dfrac{20 \times R_{eq}}{20 + R_{eq}}$

Given that $R_{eq} = 5 \Omega$, we substitute this value into the equation:
$5 = 2R + \dfrac{20 \times 5}{20 + 5}$

$5 = 2R + \dfrac{100}{25}$

$5 = 2R + 4$

$2R = 1$

$R = 0.5 \Omega$

Answer: $0.5 \Omega$

104096.subject: Physics
104096.text: Two series LCR circuits, Circuit 1 and Circuit 2, are connected to the same variable frequency AC source of peak voltage $V_0$. Circuit 1 has inductance $L$, capacitance $C$, and resistance $R$. Circuit 2 has inductance $2L$, capacitance $\dfrac{C}{2}$, and resistance $2R$. If $f_1$ and $f_2$ are their respective resonant frequencies, and $I_1$ and $I_2$ are their respective maximum peak currents at resonance, which of the following relationships is correct?
104096.sol:
The resonant frequency of a series LCR circuit is given by $f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$.

For Circuit 1: $f_1 = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$

For Circuit 2: $f_2 = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{(2L)\left(\dfrac{C}{2}\right)}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$

Thus, $f_1 = f_2$.

At resonance, the impedance of the circuit is minimum and equal to its resistance ($Z = R$). The maximum peak current is $I = \dfrac{V_0}{R}$.

For Circuit 1: $I_1 = \dfrac{V_0}{R}$

For Circuit 2: $I_2 = \dfrac{V_0}{2R} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{V_0}{R}\right) = \dfrac{I_1}{2}$

Thus, $I_1 = 2I_2$.

Answer: $f_1 = f_2$ and $I_1 = 2I_2$
